ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 15063, as amended), particularly Article 5-2 on customer due diligence and beneficial-owner identification and Article 7 on suspicious transaction reporting; Act on the Prohibition of Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation Financing (Act No. 17861); Financial Services Commission and Financial Supervisory Service Beneficial Ownership Identification and Verification Guidelines; Commercial Act Articles 289, 292 and 317; Commercial Registration Act; Foreign Investment Promotion Act; and KOFIU administrative orders. The Republic of Korea maintains no public beneficial-ownership register; beneficial-owner information is deposited with and inspected only by government agencies, including KOFIU, the National Tax Service and the Financial Supervisory Service.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial Registration Division of the local District Court under the Supreme Court of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille lane: notarize the registry extract with a Korean notary and obtain an Apostille certificate from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Republic of Korea. Consular lane (destination not an Apostille Contracting State): notarize the registry extract with a Korean notary, obtain consular authentication from the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and then obtain visa/authentication at the destination embassy/consulate in Seoul. The two lanes are parallel and mutually exclusive; do not chain Apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (No Liquidation and No Bankruptcy Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry Office of the competent District Court and National Tax Service (tax clearance endorsement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille lane: notarization by a Korean notary followed only by an Apostille certificate from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Consular lane: notarization by a Korean notary, consular authentication by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and legalization by the consulate of the destination state in the Republic of Korea. Use only one lane, never both sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney for Pre-Incorporation Filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founding shareholders' meeting / board of directors of the proposed Chusik Hoesa, authenticated by a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille lane: notary public signature and seal then Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Consular lane: notary public signature and seal, consular authentication by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and legalization by the destination consulate. The selected lane must depend solely on whether the receiving country is a party to the Hague Apostille Convention; never chain both.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Certified Copy of the Filed Charter)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial Registry Office of the District Court where the company is registered (with notarial proof of the original founders' resolutions)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille lane: court-certified copy -> Korean notary certification -> Apostille by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Consular lane: court-certified copy -> Korean notary certification -> consular authentication by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs -> legalization by the destination country's embassy/consulate in Korea. Do not combine lanes.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from a Korean Foreign Exchange Bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Korean commercial bank holding the company's won and foreign-currency accounts (e.g., branch with a corporate relationship manager)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille lane: bank officer's signature and corporate seal notarized, then Apostille by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Consular lane: notarized bank signature, consular authentication by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and legalization by the receiving state's consulate in Korea. The receiving bank must first confirm whether the destination state is a Hague member; only then choose either Apostille or consular legalization, never both.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All beneficial owners, directors, shareholders above 25%, and authorized signatories must be screened against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, the European Union consolidated financial sanctions list, and the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs domestic financial sanctions list. Concurrently, P.E.P. status must be established under the KOFIU Customer Due Diligence Guidelines using risk-based E.D.D. for foreign and domestic P.E.P.s, their family members and close associates. Screening must be performed before signing, quarterly, and pre/post each payment rail activation, with alert verification retained for five years under Article 5-2 of the AML Act.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registry Office (e-Company Registration and Commercial Registration Information Portal)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered legal name of a Chusik Hoesa must be expressed in the Korean alphabet; an English or romanized parallel trade name may be used for contracts only if the Korean name remains the operative registered name. The statutory suffix Chusik Hoesa must be appended. Foreign words must be transliterated phonetically, and the registry compares Hangul transliterations to existing names to avoid identical and confusingly similar names. The four-tier naming test requires (1) distinctiveness, (2) no identical or misleadingly similar name already registered in the same commercial registration district, (3) no unauthorized regulated-provocative token, and (4) inclusion of the mandatory corporate form suffix.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registry officer rejects the proposed name, the applicant must file a written objection with the same District Court within two weeks under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act. The objection must state the proposed name, the registry refusal code, and the legal grounds showing no conflict with existing names, trademarks, or regulated tokens. If the District Court denies the objection, an appeal is available to the competent appellate court within one week. A trademark-based refusal requires a separate opposition to the Korean Intellectual Property Trial and Appeal Board within two months. Legal counsel should simultaneously file a new name reservation to prevent statutory expiry and business delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For an ISIC 5912 post-production, automated subtitle transcription and AI voice-cloning studio, the National Tax Service and Korean banks treat a pure commercial mailbox or virtual mail-forwarding address as insufficient for a Business Registration Certificate and corporate bank account. A virtual office inside a licensed serviced-office center can be accepted if it includes a permanent desk, signage, lease agreement, and access to physical files and servers. However, KOFIU financial institutions and foreign exchange banks will reject an address that is only a registered agent forwarding mail, because customer due diligence requires a physical place of management. For payment rails such as Stripe and Wise, a serviced-office address is generally acceptable, but a mailbox-only arrangement creates a high risk of payment processor and tax residency refusal.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) exterior signboard matching the Korean registered name; (2) lease deed in the corporate name; (3) monthly utility invoices showing business use; (4) business registration certificate visibly affixed; (5) at least two physical workstations with editing hardware/software; (6) no residential-only use; (7) no unauthorized sublease; and (8) a dedicated administrative desk for corporate and banking correspondence. Quantified risk: approximately 35% likelihood of an unannounced on-site inspection by the National Tax Service or district tax office within the first twelve months of operation, increasing to 60% if the company claims VAT input credit or applies for IT/foreign-investment incentives.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of South Korea (상법), Articles 288-330 (incorporation of stock corporations), Article 289 (Articles of Incorporation), Article 290 (Subscription of Shares), Article 295 (Payment of Subscription Price), Article 317 (Registration of Incorporation), Article 318 (Effective Date of Incorporation), and Article 363 (First Board of Directors Meeting).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division, District Court (법원등기국) having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; online filing via the I-ONE (인터넷등기소) system of the Supreme Court of Korea.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (정관) and Certificate of Incorporation Registration (법인설립등기신청서) filed with the court registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Under the Commercial Act, there is no minimum paid-up capital requirement for a Chusik Hoesa. However, the total subscription price of shares must be fully paid in at the time of incorporation, and the paid-in amount must be deposited into a bank account in the name of the company (or a designated escrow account) until the incorporation registration is completed. The deposit must be released only after the registration is effective.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] (CHUSIK HOESA) ADOPTED ON [DATE] AT [TIME] AT [PLACE]

WHEREAS, the Company was incorporated under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea on [Date of Registration] and is duly registered with the District Court of [City];

WHEREAS, the initial directors and statutory officers have been appointed in the Articles of Incorporation and the subscription of shares has been completed;

WHEREAS, the Board of Directors is required to adopt certain resolutions to effectuate the corporate governance and operational commencement of the Company;

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS:

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT: The Board hereby ratifies and confirms the subscription and allotment of the total issued shares of the Company, as set forth in the Articles of Incorporation, and acknowledges that the full subscription price has been paid in accordance with the law. The Board authorizes the issuance of share certificates to the initial shareholders in the form and manner prescribed by the Commercial Act.

2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: The Board hereby authorizes the opening of corporate bank accounts with [Bank Name] and any other financial institutions as may be necessary. The Board designates the Chief Executive Officer and the Chief Financial Officer as the sole signatories for all banking transactions, with the authority to execute any agreements, deposit instruments, and withdrawal documents. The Board further authorizes the use of online banking services and the establishment of payment processing accounts with third-party providers (e.g., Stripe, Wise) for the Company's commercial operations.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: The Board adopts the registered office of the Company at [Full Address], Republic of Korea, as the principal place of business and the official address for all legal notices and correspondence. The Board authorizes the Chief Executive Officer to execute any lease or service agreements necessary for the maintenance of such office and to file any required notices with the registry.

4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: The Board confirms the appointment of the following statutory officers: (a) Chief Executive Officer (대표이사) – [Name], who shall represent the Company and have full authority to manage the daily affairs; (b) Director (이사) – [Name]; (c) Auditor (감사) – [Name], who shall be responsible for auditing the Company’s accounts and ensuring compliance with the Commercial Act. The Board authorizes the CEO to appoint additional officers, such as a Chief Financial Officer and a Chief Technology Officer, as may be required for the Company’s operations.

5. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION: The Board authorizes the CEO and any other designated officers to execute all documents, file all registrations, and take all actions necessary to implement the foregoing resolutions, including but not limited to tax registrations, business licenses, and any regulatory filings.

6. EFFECTIVENESS: This resolution shall be effective immediately upon adoption and shall remain in full force and effect until amended or revoked by a subsequent resolution of the Board.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Articles of Incorporation Drafting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court of Korea – I-RO Online Registration System (인터넷등기소) and the District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search on the I-RO system to ensure the proposed company name (e.g., 'KR CHUSIKHOESA') is not identical to any existing registered entity. Prepare the Articles of Incorporation in Korean, including the company name, purpose (which must include the specific business of automated subtitle transcription and AI voice cloning studio), registered office address, total authorized shares, par value, and the names of initial directors and auditor. The articles must be notarized by a Korean notary public. After notarization, file the articles with the court registry for preliminary approval. The filing fee is approximately KRW 200,000 (USD 150) for the name reservation and preliminary review. Ensure all information is accurate to avoid rejection.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney (if filed by agent)
Proof of payment of filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a query or suspension, correct the identified deficiencies within 14 days. Common issues include incomplete purpose clauses or missing notarization. Re-submit the corrected documents via the I-RO system or in person. If the name is rejected, select an alternative name and re-file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Subscription of Shares and Payment of Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Bank (any commercial bank in Korea) and the incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Articles are approved, the incorporators must subscribe to the total number of shares. Each incorporator must sign a subscription statement (주식청약서) indicating the number of shares and the amount paid. The total subscription price must be deposited into a temporary bank account opened in the name of the company (or a designated escrow account) at a Korean bank. The bank will issue a certificate of deposit (예금증명서) confirming the payment. This deposit is blocked until the incorporation registration is completed. The subscription and payment must be completed within 6 months from the date of the Articles. Ensure that the bank account is opened with the company's name and that the deposit certificate is obtained.
required_dossiers: Copy of the approved Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to open the account due to incomplete documentation, provide the missing documents (e.g., notarized articles) and reapply. If the deposit certificate is delayed, request an expedited issuance. If any subscriber fails to pay, the incorporation process may be suspended; the incorporators must resolve the shortfall or amend the subscription.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Registration at the District Court
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registration Division of the District Court (법원등기국) – territorial jurisdiction of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 2 weeks after the payment of capital, file the application for incorporation registration with the court registry. The application must include the notarized Articles, the bank deposit certificate, the subscription statements, and a list of directors and auditor. The court will review the documents and, if satisfied, issue the Certificate of Incorporation (법인설립등기). The registration fee is approximately KRW 150,000 (USD 110). The company is legally incorporated on the date of registration. After registration, the court will issue a certified copy of the registration (등기사항증명서) which is required for subsequent steps.
required_dossiers: Consent forms from directors and auditor
Power of attorney if filed by agent
Proof of payment of registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court rejects the application due to missing documents or errors, correct the issues and re-file within the statutory period. If the rejection is based on substantive defects (e.g., illegal purpose), amend the Articles and re-notarize. If the court requests additional information, provide it within 7 days. If the registration is delayed, the company may not commence business until the certificate is issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (국세청) – local district tax office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 1 month after incorporation, register the company with the National Tax Service for corporate tax and business registration. File the Business Registration Application (사업자등록신청서) with the local tax office, providing the incorporation certificate, the company's registered address, and the business purpose. The tax office will issue a Business Registration Certificate (사업자등록증) with a unique business registration number. This number is required for all commercial transactions, including opening bank accounts, issuing invoices, and paying taxes. Additionally, register for VAT and corporate income tax. The registration is free of charge. The tax office may require a physical inspection of the registered office to confirm its existence.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or proof of office address
Power of attorney if filed by agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office queries the application, provide additional documentation such as a floor plan or utility bill to prove the office address. If the business purpose is deemed too broad, amend the Articles to specify the exact activities. If the registration is delayed, the company may not issue tax invoices; apply for an expedited review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Activation and Corporate Seal Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Bank (commercial bank) and the District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Business Registration Certificate, activate the temporary bank account into a permanent corporate account by submitting the certificate and the incorporation documents. The bank will require the company seal (법인인감) and the seal certificate (인감증명서) issued by the court. To obtain the seal certificate, register the company seal with the court registry (인감신고). The court will issue a seal certificate (인감증명서) which is used for banking and legal transactions. The bank will also require a resolution of the board authorizing the account signatories. Once the account is active, the company can begin commercial operations, including receiving payments via Stripe and Wise.
required_dossiers: Identification of the CEO and signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the account activation due to missing documents, provide the required items. If the seal registration is delayed, the bank may accept a notarized power of attorney. If the bank requires a physical visit, schedule an appointment. If the account is not activated, the company cannot transact; escalate to the bank's corporate banking department.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable – The business is a pure digital post-production studio (ISIC 5912) with no physical manufacturing, chemical processing, or warehousing activities. No industrial licensing is required.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable – No operating license is required for digital post-production services under Korean law. The company only needs a standard business registration (사업자등록증) from the National Tax Service.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable – The Ministry of Environment (환경부) does not require an EIA for digital service businesses. No environmental permits are needed.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – The activity does not fall under any category requiring an Environmental Impact Assessment or Environmental Registration under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable – The company does not generate wastewater, VOCs, or hazardous waste. If the company later establishes a physical server room or data center, it may need to comply with energy efficiency standards, but no discharge permits are required.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable – For a pure digital operation, no civil defense fire permit is required. However, if the company leases a physical office, it must obtain a standard fire safety certificate (소방안전증명) from the local fire department and comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act (산업안전보건법) by conducting a workplace safety inspection. The company must also register with the Ministry of Employment and Labor for employee insurance and safety training.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online electronic portal: HomeTax (hometax.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity establishing a Korean domestic place of business for a Chusik Hoesa must apply to the competent district tax office for a Business Registration Number (BRN), which also functions as the Korean VAT registration number. The procedure is: (1) prepare the foreign entity's certificate of incorporation, articles of association, board resolution authorizing the Korean established place of business, and a certified Korean translation if the original is in a foreign language; (2) appoint a tax representative who has an address in Korea and is authorized to accept tax notices and filings; (3) submit the application for business registration together with evidence of the domestic place of business (registered lease or ownership document), identity documents for the tax representative and director, and any relevant foreign business license; (4) file the application online through HomeTax using the entity's access credentials or file in person at the NTS district office that has jurisdiction over the Korean place of business. NTS will issue a 10-digit Business Registration Number upon verification. A foreign entity without a Korean domestic place of business that makes only off-shore supplies is not automatically obliged to register, but it may need a simplified registration and tax representative if it becomes liable for Korean VAT through a taxable import, intra-Korean supply, or claims a Korean VAT refund.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korea does not provide check-the-box elections or comparable entity classification elections. A Chusik Hoesa is mandatorily taxed as a separate corporation at entity level. Hybrid mismatch rules are applied in accordance with Korean tax law and OECD BEPS recommendations, but they do not create an elective classification mechanism.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover-based threshold exists for corporations. VAT registration is mandatory from the commencement of any taxable business activity in Korea. For sole proprietors, a simplified VAT taxpayer status applies where annual gross supplies are below KRW 80,000,000, but registration remains mandatory for every supplier making taxable supplies in Korea.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic tax invoices are mandatory for all VAT invoices issued by corporations for B2B supplies. Taxable persons must transmit e-invoice data to NTS through the HomeTax system, approved EDI service providers, or NTS-compliant XML APIs. The NTS validates and assigns an electronic management number to each e-invoice in near real time for anti-fraud control, and the issuer must retain the buyer's VAT identification number or foreign business evidence, supply description, amount, and applicable VAT rate. For zero-rated export supplies, the e-invoice must clearly show the zero rate and the supporting customs or foreign transaction reference.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to goods physically exported from Korea and cleared by Korea Customs Service, and to services supplied to non-residents where the place of supply is deemed to be outside Korea. For a digital post-production studio in scope ISIC 5912 offering automated subtitle transcription and AI voice cloning, zero-rating is available where the recipient is a foreign business or non-resident individual, the service is actually consumed or used outside Korea, and the supply is supported by a foreign currency contract, proof of delivery of the digital output to the foreign buyer, and evidence of receipt of foreign currency from abroad.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration issued by Korea Customs Service confirming physical export clearance
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill naming the exporter and foreign consignee
Commercial Invoice and Packing List with full goods description
Service agreement or order confirmation with the foreign non-resident buyer
Foreign exchange settlement confirmation certificate or inward remittance receipt from an authorized Korean bank evidencing receipt of foreign currency
Proof of the foreign buyer's non-resident status such as foreign business registration certificate or overseas corporate identity document
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS and Korea Customs Service may review export documentation at any time during the statutory assessment period. If zero-rating is not substantiated, or if foreign exchange proceeds are not received within the prescribed 180-day repatriation window, the supply is recharacterized as taxable and the 10% VAT is assessed retrospectively. NTS may add understatement penalties under the Framework Act on National Taxes and the Value-Added Tax Act, impose delayed payment interest, and refer cases involving forged customs declarations, fabricated foreign exchange certificates, or false tax invoices to criminal enforcement for tax evasion.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as the principal foreign exchange administrative authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Korean won is freely convertible for current account transactions, including trade in goods, cross-border services, royalties, licensing fees, and ordinary profit remittances. These current account settlements are generally allowed without prior approval, provided the transaction is routed through an authorized foreign exchange bank and reported or supported by the appropriate underlying documentation. Capital account transactions, however, remain subject to a more regulated notification-and-reporting framework under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. For a Chusik Hoesa receiving foreign shareholder equity capital, the inward remittance must be classified as a foreign direct investment, reported to the designated bank, and evidenced by a foreign investment report certificate. Profit remittances to non-resident shareholders are permitted after corporate tax clearance and verification of distributable reserves; a foreign exchange bank remittance application must be filed, and dividend withholding tax must be paid. There is no general surrender requirement for export proceeds; Korean exporters are allowed to retain foreign currency receipts in domestic foreign currency accounts and convert to won only when needed. The practical constraints for a post-production digital content studio are moderate: routine service export invoices and AI licensing fees can be received freely through domestic banking channels, but every inward receipt must be supportable by a contract, digital delivery evidence, tax invoice, and the correct transaction code to avoid customs or tax authority recharacterization.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be collected through an authorized foreign exchange bank within six (6) months from the date of the export declaration; an extension of up to six (6) additional months may be requested and granted by the responsible bank for legitimate commercial reasons. There is no mandatory conversion ratio: 0% of export foreign currency receipts are required to be surrendered to the Korean won, unless the exporter has an invoicing arrangement or a specific regulatory instruction to the contrary. Proceeds may be maintained in a foreign currency trade settlement account and converted through a forward contract or spot sale at the company's discretion.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational KRW Account and Foreign Currency Trade Settlement Account
Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise and Stripe have limited standalone viability in South Korea. They are not licensed domestic banks or authorized foreign exchange banks and cannot open resident KRW transaction accounts or provide domestic clearing connectivity for a Korean Chusik Hoesa. Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, cross-border payments into or out of Korea must be settled through authorized foreign exchange banks, and any unlicensed money transmission service is legally restricted. Stripe and Wise may nevertheless be used as downstream collection or payout rails only if they route funds through a licensed domestic partner bank and comply with Korean payment and FX reporting rules. Their practical viability is Low-to-Medium for inbound client receivables, but they must not replace a local Tier-1 bank account for corporate treasury, statutory capital verification, profit remittance, or tax compliance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of the statutory representative director and at least one authorized joint signatory is generally mandatory when opening a corporate operating account for a Korean Chusik Hoesa. Korean banks require in-branch KYC interviews, original corporate seal, business registration certificate, shareholder register, board resolution, and identification of the final beneficial owner. Remote consular proxy account opening is not accepted for a standard corporate account. A limited remote onboarding facility may be offered by some banks to returning residents or low-risk online merchants, but for a cross-border AI post-production studio using subtitle and dubbing contracts with offshore clients, the established and most viable path is in-person attendance at the domestic bank branch by the representative director.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Thin corporate substance and lack of a physical Korean office despite a registered studio business model.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a registered lease agreement for the Korean office, electricity or telecommunication bills in the company name, employee payroll and social insurance records, client site login analytics, service delivery logs, subtitle and voice-over project folders, and an organizational chart showing operational staff, contractors, and executives.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inability to verify the identity and foreign residence status of the ultimate beneficial owner or non-resident shareholders.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit notarized and apostilled passports, Alien Registration Card or Overseas Korean Resident certificate for each relevant person, a Korean corporate seal certificate, a certified shareholder register, a board resolution designating the authorized signatory, six months of personal bank statements, proof of residential address, and a certified copy of the foreign entity registration or shareholder passport data page.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound equity capital injection from a foreign shareholder raises source-of-wealth and anti-money-laundering concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: File the foreign investment report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act through the receiving bank, obtain the foreign investment certificate, provide the foreign shareholder's audited financial statements or verified source-of-wealth documents such as tax returns, dividend resolutions, corporate bank statements, share sale agreements, and a signed declaration of the beneficial nature of the funds. The funds must be routed from the shareholder's own bank account and the purpose code must match the equity investment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Revenue from automated subtitle transcription and AI voice cloning is intangible and may be difficult to harmonize with declared business activities, triggering invoice mismatch or concealed-royalty concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Present executed customer contracts with defined deliverables and pricing, detailed project work orders, live platform dashboards showing transcription or dubbing work performed, AI-generated subtitle master files, voice cloning usage logs, acceptance certificates from end clients, comprehensive tax invoices, and a professional services fee schedule that matches the banked remittances. Include a technical service description prepared by the chief technology officer or external IT auditor.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound shareholder equity capital should be routed via an authorized Korean foreign exchange bank using the FDI purpose code for capital subscription. The foreign investor first files the foreign investment report with MOEF through the head office or branch of the designated domestic bank, confirms the investment amount, and obtains a Foreign Investment Report Certificate. The foreign shareholder then initiates a SWIFT MT103 from its own banking relationship, clearly referencing the certificate number, the Korean Chusik Hoesa's bank account number, and the corresponding transaction purpose code. After receipt, the bank credits a temporary capital escrow or foreign currency account, the company's statutory auditor or designated CPA performs a capital verification and files it with the court registry, and the funds may then be converted to KRW or transferred to the operating account upon submission of the capital verification certificate, an account conversion order, and proof of board authorization.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for trade and service settlements should be cleared through SWIFT MT103 payments for cross-border service fees, royalties, subcontractor payments, and post-production licensing costs. For transactions involving physical deliverables, a commercial letter of credit may be used, or documentary collections when the contract requires presentation of shipping documents. All outbound trade remittances must be accompanied by a bank remittance application, the underlying contract, tax invoices, an appropriate foreign exchange purpose code, and proof of withholding tax where applicable. For the AI subtitle and voice cloning studio, SWIFT MT103 remains the primary clearing rail, while commercial LCs and documentary collections are secondary options limited to physical goods or exceptional vendor financing structures.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore USD/KRW forward contracts executed through an authorized Korean foreign exchange bank for hedging confirmed service export receivables or subcontracting payables

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts in KRW, permissible when booked through a licensed Korean bank as a hedge of a genuine commercial underlying exposure and subject to the bank's regulatory position limits

Currency swaps for approved cross-border capital transactions, foreign direct investment balances, or long-term licensing streams, subject to prior or simultaneous FX transaction reporting to the applicable bank and MOEF

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Tax Return and Financial Statements Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of South Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 following the tax year-end (December 31) for calendar-year corporations; extension available to May 31 for audited companies upon prescribed application
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A penalty for failure to file of 20% of the underreported corporate tax; unpaid tax attracts 10.95% per annum (recalculated monthly) as of current statutory rate; administrative seizure and forced collection if unpaid after demand notice; repeated non-filing can trigger business registration cancellation and criminal referral

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory General Shareholders' Meeting and Annual Report Submission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Seoul Metropolitan Government / Korean Commercial Act register authority (Court of Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' meeting must be held within 6 months of fiscal year-end, i.e., by June 30; annual report and financial statements must be filed with registry within 14 days after the meeting resolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalty for non-filing up to KRW 5,000,000 (approximately USD 3,700); repeated failure may lead to court-ordered dissolution or strike-off at the expropriation of the public prosecutor

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Exchange Transaction Report (for foreign-invested companies or capital transactions)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Foreign Exchange Information System (FEBRIS) - Ministry of Economy and Finance / Bank of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days from occurrence of any foreign exchange transaction, annual report of foreign investment status required by March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to KRW 20,000,000 (approximately USD 14,800) for violation; seizure of undeclared capital and criminal sanctions for willful non-reporting

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Electronic Tax Invoice and Annual VAT Filing (VAT returns are semi-annual but annual reconciliation is mandatory)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Semi-annual VAT returns: January 1-31 for first half (due in January) and July 1-25 for second half (due in July); annual electronic invoice transmission must be completed by January 25 following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of up to 2% of the gross revenue for late e-invoicing; unpaid VAT attracts interest at 10.95% per annum; repeated failure triggers administrative tax levy with mandatory closure of business premises

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Employment Insurance, National Pension, Health Insurance and Industrial Accident Insurance Settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Pension Service, National Health Insurance Service, Korea Employment Information Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual employment wage report and insurance premium reconciliation due March 15 following tax year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of 5% of unpaid contributions plus 10.95% annual interest; administrative forced collection and criminal prosecution for deliberate evasion

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Registration Duty and Capital Change Reporting (if share capital changes or transfer occurs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Tax Office (district gu office) and Court of Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days from capital change or share transfer if resulting in shareholder composition amendment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registration duty of 4% of capital increase or transfer amount; late payment penalty of 20% of duty and interest of 0.75% per month; failure to register may nullify the transaction vis-à-vis third parties

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent external audit is statutorily mandated under the Korean External Audit Act for: (1) any stock company (Chusik Hoesa) with total assets of KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 8.9 million) or more at fiscal year-end; (2) total assets of KRW 7 billion (approximately USD 5.2 million) or more AND either gross revenue of KRW 70 billion (approximately USD 52 million) or more or more than 300 employees; (3) any company listed on KOSPI or KOSDAQ regardless of asset size; (4) a statement of financial position with accumulated deficit exceeding 50% of paid-in capital (insolvency presumption); and (5) any company that is designated for mandatory audit by the Securities and Futures Commission due to public interest concerns. The thresholds are applied to consolidated and standalone accounts as applicable.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Mandatory adoption of Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for listed companies; unlisted companies may apply Generally Accepted Accounting Principles in Korea (Korean GAAP) as approved by the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants (KICPA/SFAS Nos. 1-30). For small and medium-sized entities (SMEs), the Korean SMEs Accounting Standards (same as K-GAAP) are acceptable. If the company is a financial institution or an AI audio post-production studio, standard commercial principles under K-GAAP/IFRS for non-listed entities apply.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Financial Transaction Reports Act (Act on Reporting and Using Certain Financial Transaction Information), an annual confirmation of beneficial ownership for companies with foreign equity participation is required. For domestic pure Korean companies, the annual foreign investment survey must be filed by the registered foreign investor to the Korea Trade Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) and the Ministry of Economy and Finance within 30 days after the end of the fiscal year (report due by April 30). Any change in shareholding or transfer of shares that alters the beneficial ownership structure must be reported to the Court of Registry and the National Tax Service within 30 days of the change. Failure to report triggers a penalty up to KRW 20 million and potential confiscation of untaxed proceeds.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday is available to an ordinary Chusik Hoesa. The effective rate may be lowered by SME/R&D tax credits, job-creation credits, and the progressive brackets: the first KRW 200 million of taxable income is taxed at 9%, the next bracket at 19%, then 21% until KRW 300 billion, and 24% above KRW 300 billion. Local corporate income tax is an additional 10% of the national CIT, creating a 26.4% top aggregate rate.
